entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
An
Counsel for Applicant :- Praveen Kumar Yadav,Saquib Zia Khan,Satyendra Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Surendra Kumar Yadav
Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Vishwanath Nishad, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State as well as perused the material available on record.

2. This petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioners with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings of Case No. 1437 of 2022; State Vs. Lalta Prasad and Others, arising out of Case Crime No. 27 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Ghunghter, District Barabanki and chargesheet No. 1, dated 13.03.20222 as well as summoning order dated 13.12.2022 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate, court no. 27, Barabanki.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:

entities.text: Pawan Yadav And Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court referred the matter for mediation but as per mediation report dated 10.07.2023, which is on record, the mediation could not be completed as the same has been failed.

So far as the allegations against the petitioners are concerned, they are outcome of the matrimonial dispute and on the basis of submission of learned counsel for the petitioners, the proceedings in question may not be quashed/set aside at this stage, when private opposite party no. 2, who is wife of petitioner no. 1, is contesting her case continuously.
4.

Therefore, at this stage, without interfering into the proceedings pending before the learned court below, liberty is given to the petitioners to appear/surrender before the learned trial court within a period of four weeks from today by filing their bail application and if they appear/surrender and file their bail application, the same shall be disposed of expeditiously, preferably, on the same day, in the light of dictum of the Apex Court in re; Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr, Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No(s).5191/2021.
5.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is needless to say that if the learned trial court wants to seek some instructions from the prosecution, the petitioners may be enlarged on interim bail, inasmuch as in Sections under which the FIR has been lodged, they should not be taken into judicial custody.

Whereafter, the petitioners may file any appropriate application before the learned trial court at appropriate stages e.g.
application for discharge etc. and such application shall be decided by the learned trial court strictly in accordance with law by affording opportunity of hearing to the parties concerned by speaking and reasoned order.
6. In view of the above, the petition is disposed of.

[Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.] Order Date :- 12.3.2024 kkv/
